answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with surprise gale windows: each epoch a random slice of identities must re-prove itself within minutes, doing fresh non-parallelizable work tied to a recent useful contribution. Like light through a prism, an agent record splits into verifiable facets (work, timing, and peers) that a farm cannot fake in bulk. The delta is stark: an honest agent passes cheaply because it is already active, while a farm must pay full compute for every fake in the same narrow window, so its cost scales with its size and its fakes starve.
